I am a 53-year-old woman from Dongwangbao village in Houcun township. I have been farming since I was 23 years old — 30 years now. I never went to school, so I cannot read or write. Everything I know about farming I learned from my parents, from my own fields, and from watching the neighbors.

My family has 5 people. My husband and I farm, and our children help when they can, but some of them work outside now, so I cannot count on them for the busy season. I have 60 mu of land. I plant 20 mu with wheat and then maize after the wheat comes off, and the other 40 mu I plant with cotton. This is what I have always done. The wheat-maize gives us grain and stable income, and cotton makes more money per mu, but it needs so much work.

It is now spring. My wheat went in the ground last October around the 2nd, and it is growing now. I need to topdress it soon. Last year I put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and then another bag and a half at jointing time. The wheat looked good and I got about 1000 jin per mu, so I will do the same this year. I use the government seed — it is reliable and the price is okay. I irrigate three times for wheat: once in spring before it turns green, once at jointing, and once at filling. Water costs money — about 30 yuan per mu for the season — but without it the wheat will not make it through the dry spring here on the North China Plain. I also spray for insects twice and for weeds once. The aphids always come. My neighbor's wheat got rust last year so I also spray a little fungicide just in case. I hire a tractor for rotary tillage before planting and a combine for harvest. Sowing and harvest I pay others to do — 35 yuan for sowing, 50 for harvest — because my family does not have the machines.

For cotton, I will plant around April 15th. I grow the 99ganong variety. It costs about 52 yuan per mu for seed. Cotton needs a lot of fertilizer — I put down almost two bags of compound per mu before planting, and then topdress with urea once when the plants are growing strong. The cotton bolls need nitrogen. I irrigate once, usually around flowering time. But cotton's real problem is insects. Last year I sprayed 12 times! The bollworms never stop. That costs a lot — over 200 yuan per mu just for insecticide. I also spray herbicide once. For cotton I do rotary tillage before planting. The picking is the hardest part. My family picks most of it — it takes us many days — but I hire a few people for about 12-13 days to help because 40 mu is too much for us alone.

For maize, I plant right after the wheat comes off, around June 5th. There is almost no time between harvest and planting — sometimes less than a week. So I do not till. I just plant directly into the wheat stubble. I use hybrid seed — about 82 yuan per mu. I put down about one and a half bags of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. Maize does not need as much as cotton, and I do not topdress it — there is no time and the compound at planting is enough. I irrigate once, usually if the summer gets dry. I spray for insects twice and weeds once. Harvest is around October 2nd. I hire a combine for that — 50 yuan per mu.

Why do I do it this way? Because this is what works. I have tried to change things before and it never goes well. Last year the prices were okay — wheat about 1.08 yuan per jin, maize about 0.85, cotton about 3.05. I need the cash from all three crops. Cotton brings the most money but costs the most too, especially for spraying. Wheat and maize are my insurance — even if cotton fails, we still have grain to eat and sell.

I do not have money to waste. I buy what I need, not what the extension people say is "optimal." I know my land. Some years I could use more fertilizer, but if I spend too much on inputs and then the price drops or there is a drought, I am in trouble. I would rather put a little too much fertilizer than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps. But I also need cash in my pocket for emergencies. My husband and I are getting older. We cannot work like we used to. That is why I hire help for harvest and cotton picking.
